data.summary: Candidate action diversity at rollout time is ~9.5 deg mean (min 0.006, max 30 deg), measured as 1-cos to the candidate mean over K=4 samples per replan step across a full PnPCounterToSink episode with GR00T N1.6. This is 15x smaller than the 150 deg spread measured earlier on a SYNTHETIC single-frame probe input. In-distribution, with real state and video history, the flow-matching sampler is confident. Selection among K samples of the same observation therefore has almost nothing to choose between.

Action and frame conventions verified empirically, not assumed. (1) default_pandaomron.json sets arms.right.type=OSC_POSE with input_type=delta and input_ref_frame=base, so action.end_effector_position is a BASE-FRAME DELTA -- the checkpoint's rep=ABSOLUTE describes GR00T's normalisation, not the controller. (2) state.end_effector_position_absolute equals the sim grip site exactly ([3.0463,-0.55,1.2928]), so 'absolute' is world frame. (3) base_rotation is xyzw ([0,0,0.7071,0.7071]) and R(base_rotation)^T @ (abs - base_position) reproduces end_effector_position_relative with error 0.00000, giving an exact world->base transform. Also: GR00T's wrapper image is the vertical flip of a raw MuJoCo render (mean|diff| 1.2 flipped vs 93 unflipped) and cameras render at 512 while the policy consumes downsampled 256 copies -- both calibrated per camera rather than assumed.

GR00T's served policy exposes no sampling-diversity control. Gr00tPolicy.get_action documents its options parameter as 'currently unused' (gr00t/policy/gr00t_policy.py:320 and :580), and run_gr00t_server.py's ServerConfig has no temperature, cfg_scale, denoising-steps or noise-scale field. Diversity therefore cannot be raised through the server API without modifying model or server code.

GPU capacity and thermals measured on the DGX Spark (GB10, aarch64, sm_121). (1) An inference server and a 3B fine-tune cannot coexist: with openpi's JAX server holding the GPU, a 1024x1024 bf16 matmul in a separate torch process failed with 'CUDA error: out of memory' on a 121 GB unified-memory machine; stopping the server made the same op succeed. (2) Under sustained training the SoC ACPI zones reach 88 C while the GPU die reads 80 C, with SW power capping already engaged and SM clocks at 2483 of 3003 MHz. nvidia-smi reports every power-limit field as N/A and 'nvidia-smi -lgc' is refused for a non-root user, so the only available lever is pausing the trainer. A SIGSTOP/SIGCONT governor at an 80 C ceiling holds the SoC near 80 C at 4.32 s/step against 2.77 uncooled (~64% throughput).

data.rationale: Frames and conventions are calibrated rather than assumed, and each calibration is checked against a ground truth: world frame confirmed by equality with the sim grip site, world->base transform reproduces the reported relative state to 0.00000, camera orientation chosen by comparing a re-render against the wrapper's own image under all four flips (and raising if none wins), and boxes measured at the cameras' native 512 then scaled into the 256 frame the policy consumes.

REFUTED by measurement. In-distribution candidate spread is ~9.5 deg mean (max 30), not the 150 deg the selection approach was premised on; the 150 came from a synthetic single-frame probe input and does not hold at rollout. Combined with C-0003 (no temperature knob), same-observation K-sampling cannot supply the diversity selection requires, so the selection design as built is not viable. This does NOT rule out selection per se: MG-Select's actual mechanism is input PERTURBATION (randomly masked states and language), which is untried here and needs its own measurement.

Resolved as a known limitation rather than an open question: the server exposes no diversity control, confirmed by reading the served policy and the server config. Any approach needing more sampling diversity must obtain it outside the API (input perturbation) or by modifying third_party code.

Measured and now designed around: serving and training cannot share this GPU, so scripts/finetune_overlay.sh stops any running inference server before training, and evaluation requires stopping the trainer (resume from the newest checkpoint is automatic).

Thermal envelope characterised and mitigated within the levers available to a non-root user: the SIGSTOP/SIGCONT governor holds the SoC near 80 C at ~64% throughput. Note the mitigation is throughput-for-heat, not free; a root-level clock cap (nvidia-smi -lgc) would be strictly better and remains unavailable.

data.title: Establish a trustworthy rollout baseline: verify episode accounting and scene pinning, then measure the ungrounded success rate

data.rationale: Re-scoped, not excused. C-0001 was written as a project-level hard constraint but is actually a precondition of ONE approach: selecting among K samples drawn from the same observation. EV-0001 refuted that precondition (9.5 deg in-distribution vs the 150 deg it assumed) and EV-0003 showed the diversity cannot be raised through the server API, so that approach is abandoned rather than pending -- which is precisely what not_applicable means here. The measurement stands permanently as EV-0001 and the selection code remains committed at c330902 as a record. If input-perturbation selection (MG-Select's actual mechanism: randomly masked states and language) is ever attempted, it needs its OWN constraint and its own measurement; it must not inherit this one's resolution.

data.title: Establish a trustworthy rollout baseline: verify episode accounting and scene pinning, then measure the ungrounded success rate
Establish a trustworthy rollout baseline: verify episode accounting and scene pinning, then measure the ungrounded success rate

data.note: Approved by the human (nickname "the Craftman") in-session. Scope: read-only measurement -- serve base GR00T-N1.6-3B, two ungrounded K=1 rollouts on pinned scenes (PnPCounterToSink, layout 1 / style 1 / seed 0, 15 episodes each) to resolve C-0002 (episode/success accounting) and C-0004 (scene pinning) and establish the baseline for G2/G3. No weights, datasets or checkpoints touched; the fine-tune resumes from checkpoint-2000 when restarted.

data.summary: C-0002 RESOLVED, and the bug was mine, not the harness's. run_rollout_gymnasium_policy returns a TUPLE (env_name, [bool per episode], info). For 15 requested episodes it returned exactly 15 booleans in both runs, so the harness counts correctly. The '2/3 successes for 1 episode' symptom came from client-side extraction in rollout_select.py/rollout_overlay.py, which fell through to 'succ = results' for any tuple and thus scored the truthiness of a string, a list and an empty dict -> a constant 66.7% (2/3) regardless of what the robot did. Both runners now locate the boolean sequence explicitly and raise if they cannot, instead of silently scoring the wrong object. The two artifacts were corrected in place from the raw harness output.

C-0004 RESOLVED: scene pinning holds. Two independent processes with identical --layout 1 --style-id 1 --scene-seed 0 traversed a byte-identical 17-entry scene sequence (wine, corn, garlic, kettle non electric, cup, pan, garlic, pear, can, lime, ketchup, banana, kiwi, orange, spray, mug), recorded at every env reset rather than inferred from the settings passed in. Note two things this does NOT mean: the object instance varies per EPISODE within a run (each episode draws a different target), and per-episode outcomes still differ between the two runs (run1 and run2 succeeded on different episodes despite identical scenes) because the policy is stochastic. So arms can be paired scene-for-scene, but paired comparison still has to average over policy noise.

BASELINE ESTABLISHED for G2/G3. Ungrounded GR00T N1.6 (K=1, no selection, no overlay) on RoboCasa PnPCounterToSink, scenes pinned: 8/15 = 53.3% in BOTH independent runs, Wilson 95% CI [30.1%, 75.2%]. The interval contains NVIDIA's published 46.0% zero-shot figure, so the serving and observation pipeline reproduces the published behaviour and the harness can be trusted for comparisons. The CI is wide at n=15: a grounded arm would need roughly a 25-30 point improvement to clear it at this sample size, so any future comparison should either raise n substantially or use a paired per-scene test rather than comparing marginal rates.

data.rationale: The harness counts correctly: 15 booleans returned for 15 requested episodes, in two independent runs. The 2/3-for-1-episode symptom that raised this constraint was a client-side extraction bug in our own runners, now fixed to locate the boolean sequence explicitly and raise rather than silently score the wrong object. Artifacts corrected in place from the raw harness output.

Verified by construction rather than by settings: two independent processes with identical layout/style/seed traversed a byte-identical 17-entry scene sequence, recorded at each env reset. Arms can therefore be paired scene-for-scene. Caveat carried forward: the target object varies per episode within a run, and identical scenes still produce different per-episode outcomes because the policy is stochastic, so paired comparison must average over policy noise.

data.summary: All three adopt_if conditions hold, though one required a repair inside the plan's allowed files first. (1) ACCOUNTING: the harness returned exactly 15 booleans for 15 requested episodes in both runs -- it counts correctly. The 2/3-for-1-episode symptom that motivated this plan was a client-side extraction bug in our own runners, which scored the truthiness of (env_name, successes, info) and produced a constant 66.7% regardless of robot behaviour; both runners now extract explicitly and raise rather than score the wrong object, and the artifacts were corrected from the raw output. Strictly, reject_if ('episode counts disagree with the request') fired on the FIRST reading -- that reading was the defect this measurement was designed to expose, it was localised to two allowed files, and the corrected reading satisfies adopt_if. (2) PINNING: two independent processes traversed a byte-identical 17-entry scene sequence. (3) BASELINE: 8/15 = 53.3% in both runs, Wilson 95% CI [30.1%, 75.2%], containing the published 46.0%. Baseline for G2/G3 is 53.3% (n=15, pinned). Carried forward: the CI is wide enough that a grounded arm would need ~25-30 points to clear it at n=15, so future comparisons need a larger n or a paired per-scene test; and the extraction bug never touched the checkpoint-1000 evaluation, which used the probe rather than this harness.

data.title: Screen the overlay fine-tune at checkpoint-2000: does it preserve ungrounded behaviour, and does the mark buy anything yet?

data.note: Approved in-session by the human (nickname "the Craftman"), responding "sure" to the drafted plan. Scope: read-only measurement -- serve checkpoints/groot_overlay/checkpoint-2000 and run two 15-episode arms (overlay off, overlay on) on pinned scenes, paired against the committed 53.3% baseline. No training, dataset or checkpoint changes.

data.summary: PRESERVATION FAILED, decisively. checkpoint-2000 scored 0/15 with the overlay OFF and 0/15 with it ON, against a committed base-model baseline of 8/15 (53.3%, CI [30.1%, 75.2%]) on the same pinned scenes through the same code path. 2000 steps of fine-tuning did not merely fail to help -- it destroyed the policy on this task. Ruled out as causes: (a) serving the wrong weights -- the server log names checkpoint-2000 explicitly; (b) a normalization artifact -- action.end_effector_position, end_effector_rotation and gripper_close statistics are BYTE-IDENTICAL between the checkpoint and the base model; (c) an extraction bug -- both artifacts record 15 booleans for 15 episodes through the runner fixed in EV-0005. The overlay arm being equally dead means the mark cannot rescue a broken policy, which is uninformative about grounding.

PROBABLE CAUSE of the collapse, and it is a defect in OUR data pipeline rather than in Point-VLA's recipe. examples/emit_lerobot.py writes timestamps as arange(n)/FPS with FPS=20 and declares fps=20 in meta/info.json, but the dataset was emitted with --stride 4 over 20 Hz RoboCasa demos. Consecutive rows are therefore 4 sim steps (0.2 s) apart in reality while being labelled 0.05 s apart -- a dataset that is actually 5 Hz masquerading as 20 Hz. With the checkpoint's 16-step action horizon, training chunks span 64 sim steps (~3.2 s) of real motion while an inference chunk is executed over 16 steps (~0.8 s): a 4x temporal mismatch, which is sufficient on its own to produce total failure. This was invisible in the loss curve and is exactly the class of defect that trains cleanly and evaluates as noise. NOT YET PROVEN to be the sole cause -- a 3B full fine-tune at lr 1e-4 on 55 single-task demos could also overfit destructively -- but it must be fixed before any conclusion about the recipe is drawn from this run.

reject_if fired unambiguously: the ungrounded arm scored 0/15 (0%), far below the baseline CI floor of 30.1%. Co-training has not preserved ungrounded behaviour at 2000 steps -- the fine-tune destroyed the policy, taking it from 53.3% to zero on identical pinned scenes. The overlay arm was also 0/15, which says nothing about grounding: a mark cannot rescue a policy that no longer acts. Per the rule, training STOPS rather than continuing toward 10000 steps; the screen did its job and saved roughly 8 GPU hours. Three alternative explanations were checked and eliminated (wrong weights served, normalization drift, extraction bug -- see EV-0008). A concrete probable cause was found instead, in our own pipeline rather than in the recipe (EV-0009): the dataset declares 20 Hz while being emitted at --stride 4 over 20 Hz demos, so it is really 5 Hz mislabelled, and against a 16-step action horizon that is a 4x temporal mismatch between training and inference. IMPORTANT SCOPE NOTE: this outcome rejects THIS TRAINING RUN, not Point-VLA's recipe. No conclusion about overlay fine-tuning can be drawn until the dataset is re-emitted with consistent temporal spacing and the run repeated.

data.approver: David Chen (delegated to damped-loop, standing approval 2026-08-17)
data.note: Approved under the standing delegation after plan-reviewer returned VERDICT: APPROVE-RECOMMENDED on version 4 with no required repairs. Version 5 differs from the reviewed version 4 ONLY by the three text-only corrections the reviewer itself dictated as its condition of approval: (1) the null SD of D corrected from 3.86 (unpaired two-independent-binomials model, inapplicable when the baseline is fixed and committed) to approximately 2.4, at most 2.74 by construction, with the screen restated as conservative (approximately 10% false-positive rate, approximately 80% power at +20 points) rather than permissive, in decision_rule.adopt_if and V-006; (2) the "expected n_nonzero about 1" figure qualified as the deterministic-scene model with the 1/5/11 range across scene models stated, so a run returning n_nonzero near 5 does not read as falsifying the pre-registration, in the hypothesis and V-005; (3) C-0007's not_applicable status prefaced with an explicit reading instruction that inference-regime thermal exposure is UNMEASURED and is being measured by V-002, not that the constraint does not apply. Nothing about what is run, recorded or decided differs between versions 4 and 5. Design choice between the powered 4-runs-per-arm option and this exploratory 2-runs-per-arm screen was made directly by David Chen on 2026-08-18. Two repair rounds were used, which is the maximum; a third would have ended autonomy.

data.summary: OVERLAY-ON vs BASELINE ON THE BASE MODEL, PAIRED PER SCENE: D = -2 episodes out of 30, BELOW the pre-registered screen threshold of 4. Base nvidia/GR00T-N1.6-3B served (V-001: log line 'Model path: nvidia/GR00T-N1.6-3B', no checkpoints/ path). Two overlay runs of 15 episodes on pinned scenes (layout 1, style 1, seed 0) returned 7/15 and 7/15 = 14/30 = 46.7%, against the committed baseline's 8/15 and 8/15 = 16/30 = 53.3%. Wilson 95% intervals, DESCRIPTIVE ONLY: overlay [30.2%, 63.9%], baseline [36.1%, 69.8%]. V-004 PASS: the 17-entry scene sequence is identical across all four runs, so the arms are genuinely paired. Per-scene b = [0,0,2,0,2,0,0,2,0,2,1,2,1,2,2], o = [0,2,0,0,0,0,1,2,0,2,2,2,1,1,1], d = [0,2,-2,0,-2,0,1,0,0,0,1,0,0,-1,-1]; n_nonzero = 7, with 3 scenes improving, 4 worsening and 8 unchanged. n_nonzero = 7 sits between this plan's deterministic-scene (about 1) and shrunk-difficulty (about 5) models and does NOT contradict the pre-registered power analysis, which holds across all three scene models. NO SIGNIFICANCE TEST WAS RUN, as pre-registered. V-002/V-003 PASS on every criterion and this is the first overlay run in this project that PROVES the mark reached the policy rather than asserting it: run 1 painted 14832 frames and skipped 6802, run 2 painted 16409 and skipped 5225, both with painted + skipped = 21634 = 2 x (10800 steps + 17 resets) exactly; painted fractions 0.686 and 0.758 (>= 0.5 required); mean box area fractions 0.00436 and 0.00424 of the 256 frame (> 0 required). The residual skips are occlusion (box is None), the only skip path that can fire. INTERPRETATION, STATED AS THE PLAN REQUIRES: no effect detectable at this budget (screen threshold 4 episodes; null SD of D approximately 2.4 episodes, at most 2.74 by construction conditional on the committed baseline; screen false-positive rate approximately 10%, power approximately 80% at a true +20-point effect). THIS IS NOT EVIDENCE THAT THE MARK IS INERT -- this design has no power to establish that. The observed direction is mildly negative, which is consistent with the plan's stated occlusion concern but far too small to distinguish from noise at |D| = 2.

C-0007 UNDER INFERENCE, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. Thermal zones sampled every 20 s through both 15-episode overlay rollouts (47 samples each, ~15.5 min per run, ~62 s per episode) while the GR00T server held the GPU and no trainer ran. Run 1 peaked at SoC 72.4 C / GPU 64 C; run 2 at SoC 74.1 C / GPU 73 C. Idle before the runs was SoC 43.7 C / GPU 37-43 C. This is well inside the envelope: EV-0004 recorded SoC 88 C under SUSTAINED TRAINING, which is what forced the thermal governor. Inference-only evaluation at this cadence needs no governor and no duty cycling. THIS RECORD EXISTS BECAUSE AN EARLIER VERSION OF THE PLAN'S CONSTRAINT AUDIT CITED 'EV-0004: inference-only rollouts measured 58-71 C', a figure that appears in no evidence record in this project. That citation was fabricated and was withdrawn during review; these are the first real inference-regime numbers, and they are close to but not equal to the invented range, which is precisely why an invented range is not acceptable as evidence.

Plan ran exactly as pre-registered and its reject_if branch fired. D = -2 episodes out of 30 (overlay 14/30 = 46.7%, baseline 16/30 = 53.3%), so |D| = 2 <= 3 and the powered 4-runs-per-arm follow-up is NOT commissioned. Polarity neutral, recorded per V-006 as 'no effect detectable at this budget' and explicitly NOT as 'the mark is inert', which this design has no power to establish. 'validated' here means the MEASUREMENT executed and its pre-registered rule was applied without deviation -- not that the overlay was shown to work. All five required validation steps passed: V-001 confirmed base nvidia/GR00T-N1.6-3B weights with no checkpoints/ path; V-002 and V-003 confirmed the mark actually reached the policy (painted 14832 and 16409 frames, painted fractions 0.686 and 0.758, mean box area 0.0044 of the 256 frame, and the accounting identity painted + skipped = 21634 = 2 x (10800 steps + 17 resets) exact in both runs); V-004 confirmed the 17-entry scene sequence is identical across all four runs so the arms are genuinely paired; V-005 reported the per-scene contingency (3 improved, 4 worsened, 8 unchanged, n_nonzero = 7) with no significance test, as pre-registered. NO N-HACKING: the result fell cleanly in reject_if, no re-runs were performed, and no post-hoc test was applied to the 7 nonzero pairs. WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT ESTABLISH. It does not establish that a training-free oracle overlay helps, hurts, or does nothing; at 2 runs per arm the screen would miss any effect below roughly 20 points. It does establish, for the first time in this project, that the overlay pipeline genuinely paints the target into the frames the policy consumes during a live rollout -- previous overlay runs asserted this from a console line printed before any episode began, which is how the 0/15 ckpt2000 result was indistinguishable from 'nothing was painted'. Combined with the probe results (mark relocation 9.8-27.8 deg, inert-to-ambiguous), the picture is consistent: an untrained policy is not visibly steered by a 0.44%-of-frame outline, and any Point-VLA-style gain would have to come from fine-tuning on overlaid frames, not from the mark alone. PROCESS NOTE WORTH KEEPING: this plan needed both permitted repair rounds. Round 1 introduced a paired exact Wilcoxon as the primary test and claimed it was 'where the power actually is'; review showed it had realized alpha 0.000-0.003 rather than 0.05 and was LESS able to decide than the marginal comparison it replaced, and that about 47% of its significant results would have satisfied neither decision branch. Round 1 also carried a fabricated citation attributing an inference thermal range to EV-0004. Round 2 withdrew both, dropped hypothesis testing entirely at David Chen's direction, and replaced it with this screen. EV-0011 now supplies the real inference thermals the fabricated citation had invented.
